rule.body: An idiom means something different from its separate words, so never pick the literal meaning: "bury the hatchet" is about making peace, not digging. For phrasal verbs, the small particle (off, up, out, on) changes the meaning completely, so learn each one as a whole: call off means cancel, put up with means tolerate. Test your choice by putting it back into the sentence.
rule.example: The match was **called off** (cancelled) because of the rain.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the underlined expression: With the exam a week away, Halima has been [[burning the midnight oil]].
questions.explanation: To "burn the midnight oil" means to work or study until late at night.

questions.stem: The football match was ___ because of the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: To "call off" an event means to cancel it.

questions.stem: We have ___ sugar, so I must go to the shop.
questions.explanation: To "run out of" something means to use it all up so that none is left.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the underlined expression: The new stadium has become [[a white elephant]]; it cost billions but is hardly ever used.

options.A: a costly thing that is of little use

questions.explanation: A "white elephant" is something that costs a lot to build or keep but brings little benefit.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the underlined expression: After years of quarrelling, the two families decided to [[bury the hatchet]].
questions.explanation: To "bury the hatchet" means to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the underlined expression: Nobody was supposed to know about the surprise party, but Dayo [[let the cat out of the bag]].
questions.explanation: To "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret, often by mistake.

questions.stem: I cannot ___ his rudeness any longer.
questions.explanation: To "put up with" something means to tolerate or bear it.

questions.stem: Obi is so arrogant that he ___ classmates who cannot afford expensive phones.
questions.explanation: To "look down on" people means to treat them as less important than you, which is what an arrogant person does.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best explains the underlined expression: The government [[turned a deaf ear]] to the workers' demands, so the strike continued.
questions.explanation: To "turn a deaf ear" means to deliberately ignore a request. It is not about being unable to hear.

questions.stem: Tunde worked extra hours on Saturday to ___ the time he had lost during the week.
questions.explanation: To "make up for" something means to do something good to balance a loss or mistake.
